items.title: How the US-Iran war has redrawn Asia's energy map
Will the US-Iran war and Hormuz deadlock last for months?
items.description: Will the war on Iran and Hormuz deadlock last for months? Experts analyse the obstacles blocking a lasting deal.

items.title: Africa and the ICC: Why most countries are staying
items.description: A new wave of African withdrawals has swept through the International Criminal Court. Chad turned its back on the court after three junta-led states in the Sahel exited. But most African countries still trust The Hague.

items.description: Miliband, 'continua la pressione su Russia fino a pace giusta e duratura'

items.title: Human rights organizations call for war crime probe into Israel's killing of Lebanese journalist
items.description: According to Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch, the Israeli army had several indicators to identify Amal Khalil, a journalist for 'Al-Akhbar,' a left-wing daily close to Hezbollah, who was killed on April 22.

items.title: UN warns drone attacks have become leading cause of civilian death in Sudan
items.description: The UN says drone attacks have become the leading cause of death in Sudan, accounting for 80% of civilian casualties during the first four months of 2026. Sudan plunged into all-out war in April 2023, between the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and the Sudanese military, leaving at least 59,000 people killed, a…

items.title: Israeli strike that killed journalist in Lebanon was war crime, say rights groups
items.description: Investigation by Human Rights Watch, Amnesty and Legal Agenda shows Israel deliberately attacked Amal Khalil and colleague Zeinab Faraj knowing they were civiliansAn Israeli strike that killed Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil and injured her colleague Zeinab Faraj in April was a war crime, three rights organisations sai…

items.title: Israel strikes south Lebanon after two soldiers killed by explosion
items.description: Lebanese authorities says one person was killed in the strikes, which came after the first Israeli military fatalities in Lebanon in more than a month.

items.title: ‘There were many of them, and the grass was tall’: 505 nights under Russian fire
items.description: Many soldiers in Ukraine are spending long periods on the front lines, as Ukraine struggles against Russia’s numerical advantage. One infantryman, in the trenches for nearly a year and a half straight, tells us his story.

items.title: Can ‘Russia’s Amazon’ Survive Ukraine’s Drone Campaign?
items.description: Russia’s online retail sector has thrived since the invasion of Ukraine. The attacks on Wildberries now threaten to disrupt that growth.

items.title: EU Chief Slams Russian ‘Atrocities’ After Kyiv Attack
items.description: EU chief Ursula von der Leyen condemned Russia’s latest deadly attack on Kyiv and said Ukraine will receive another €1.4 billion in profits generated from frozen Russian assets. The funds are part of a broader EU effort to make Moscow pay for its war and support Ukraine’s defense.

items.title: US Senator Rick Scott: Putin 'Underestimated Trump's Commitment To Freedom'
items.description: In an interview with RFE/RL, Republican Senator Rick Scott said Russian President Vladimir Putin did not anticipate the strength of US support for Ukraine's war effort, adding that a new sanctions bill is meant to hold Russia accountable.

items.title: Gaza ‘unsafe for civilians’ as Israeli attacks hit homes and classrooms
items.description: Gaza remains unsafe for civilians as Israeli attacks continue, including on schools and canvas classrooms, despite the October Israel-Hamas ceasefire that ended two years of war, the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) warned on Tuesday.
